instruction: Type "Chapter 1" as the title on slide 3 and set the font to "Liberation Sans".

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully inserted title 'Happy Family' on slide 1 and changed font to Microsoft JhengHei. Used terminal to verify font availability, then typed text and set font in LibreOffice Impress.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click on title placeholder, type text, change font via font selector, use terminal for font verification, navigate between slides in LibreOffice Impress UI
metadata.task_rationale: Tests navigation to a different slide (slide 3 instead of slide 1) and uses a different common font (Liberation Sans). Adds complexity by requiring slide navigation while keeping the same text + font pattern.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to slide 3, typing title text, and setting font to Liberation Sans. Getter extracts title text and font name from slide 3 (index 2). Metric gives 0.5 for correct text and 0.5 for correct font name.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets slide index 2 (slide 3, 0-indexed) and extracts title placeholder (type 1) text and font name
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as direct rules dict (proper type='rule' handling), accessing expected.get('expected_text') and expected.get('expected_font_name') directly
Both instruction requirements are verified: title text 'Chapter 1' (0.5) and font 'Liberation Sans' (0.5), with appropriate partial credit
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state
Case-insensitive comparison is appropriate for both text and font name matching
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter only reads font from run.font.name; if font is inherited from paragraph/slide master level and not explicitly set on the run, it may return None. Consider falling back to paragraph-level or shape-level font detection.
